subject: ZenLeaf: committed capacity projection — KV cache & quantization impact
messages:

Cc: procurement@zenleaf.com
Date: Fri, 25 May 2028 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Sizing for the long-context med model (commit ask)

Hi Rafael / Grace,

Thanks for the call this morning — appreciate the walkthrough. A couple of follow-ups from ZenLeaf Ops and procurement as we move toward a commitment: 1) We need a concise committed-capacity projection (monthly GPUs / reserved pods) that shows options with and without model quantization for our 65B medical assistant model (med-65B-32k). 2) Our workloads will have long recall windows — typical conversations hit 20k–30k tokens (rarely up to 40k). We need to understand KV cache footprint per concurrent session and how that scales with quantization levels.

Can you send a short pro forma (not the final contract) that shows conservative headroom for peak trading (50 concurrent sessions) and an optimized configuration assuming NF4 quantization? Procurement also asked for an attachment-friendly spreadsheet.

Thanks,
Lydia

Hi Lydia — thanks, will do. Attaching a first-pass sizing workbook (zenleaf_dedicated_sizing_v2.xlsx) and the profiling dump we used on your sample traces (zenleaf_profile_dump_20280523.tar.gz).

High-level summary up front (TL;DR):
- Baseline (FP16 weights): larger per-GPU weight residency and higher memory for KV cache. For med-65B-32k we estimate approx 2.0–2.6 GB of KV cache per concurrent session at 32k context (depends on layer size / attention implementation).
- NF4/int8 quantization reduces model resident weight footprint by ~2.0–2.8x in our inference tests, which in turn reduces the number of reserved pods required for the same concurrency by roughly the same factor (subject to TP/DP sharding constraints).
- Recommendation: If ZenLeaf is comfortable with NF4 for production inference on this model, committed capacity can be sized about 40–55% lower vs FP16 baseline for the steady-state QPS profile you shared. We show three commitment tiers in the sheet (Conservative / Balanced / Optimized).

Next steps: Priyom will add a short per-token KV table and a blended monthly cost estimate. Grace — can you confirm SLA/start date options so I can bake uptime headroom into the projection?

-Rafael

Subject: Re: Sizing for the long-context med model (commit ask)

Rafael / Grace / Lydia — I reviewed the traces and the profiling dump. Pulling out the technical points so procurement can see the assumptions clearly: 

1) KV cache sizing (approx, per concurrent session):
   - 16k context: ~1.0–1.3 GB KV cache
   - 32k context: ~2.0–2.6 GB KV cache
   - 40k context: ~2.5–3.3 GB KV cache
   *These numbers assume our optimized KV layout (packed keys/values, 4-byte tokens per vector element in baseline). Your model's hidden dim (~8k) is the primary driver here.

2) Model resident weights on GPU (effective working set):
   - FP16 baseline: large working set; in our orchestration pattern this maps to higher per-GPU residency and thus more pods for the same concurrency.
   - NF4 (inference quantization): reduces resident weight by ~2.3x on average in our calibration runs for med-65B-32k, with minimal observed quality drop on your eval prompts (~<1.5% delta on key QA metrics).

3) Example committed-capacity buckets (rounded):
   - Conservative (no quantization, FP16): target 12 reserved pods (80GB-class GPUs) to sustain 50 concurrent sessions with 20–30k avg context and 15% headroom.
   - Balanced (NF4 for weights, keep KV in 16-bit packing): target 7 reserved pods (same GPU class) for same load.
   - Optimized (NF4 + KV compression knobs enabled): target 5–6 reserved pods.

4) Operational notes:
   - KV cache scales linearly per concurrent session — caching prefixes helps if many sessions share history.
   - Quantization changes mean we should test a small canary (5–10% traffic) for 2 weeks before ramping. We'll provide a regression deck.

I added the per-token rows and a cost calculator into the workbook. The profiling dump contains the sample traces we used; you'll see the per-request memory waterfall in /profiles/memory_walkthrough.html inside the tar.

-Priyom

- For the Balanced bucket (7 pods), what is the expected 99th percentile latency for a 30k token generation vs the FP16 Conservative bucket?

Lydia / team — answers inline and a short contract-ready paragraph below.

- SKU: We used 80GB H100-class equivalence for the reserved pod math (the workbook includes a column tying pods to our internal SKU codes and an approximate hourly rate).
- 99p latency comparison (rough): for a 30k token generation at same output sampling settings, Balanced (NF4) is ~1.05–1.15x the 99p of Conservative (FP16) in our measurements — i.e., a small latency increase driven by dequantization steps and slightly higher kernel counts, but still within most SLAs. We included percentile numbers in the sheet under the "perf_estimates" tab.

Contract paragraph (copy/paste):
"Capacity assumptions: Sizing is based on med-65B-32k performance profiles produced from ZenLeaf sample traces dated 2028-05-23. The parties agree the baseline (Conservative) assumes FP16 resident weights and projects 12 reserved H100-equivalent pods to support 50 concurrent sessions with 15% operational headroom. The Balanced option assumes NF4 weight quantization and projects 7 reserved H100-equivalent pods for the same workload. KV cache is modeled linearly at ~2.2 GB per concurrent session for 32k average context; actual KV usage will vary per conversation shape. Redwood will run a 2-week canary on NF4 for production inference prior to full traffic ramp; material regressions >3% on agreed QA metrics will trigger rollback. Pricing for each tier is set out in Exhibit A (per-pod monthly commitment)."

Next steps from our side: finalize Exhibit A pricing, Grace to confirm start date and SLA tier, and schedule the canary kickoff window.

Thanks — will stand by for procurement doc updates.

-Rafael
